title: Empirical Likelihood and Exponential Tilting under Critical Weak Overlap with Pareto Tails
banked_reason: Validity-gate-confirmed proposal-stage below-floor stop after two REVISE reviews: fixed mathematical estimator-safety benchmark remains letter/subfield rather than field. Operator override banks downgraded. Claims remain unproved; no D0 derivation or Lean formalization ran.
gap_reasons: Their consumers are only a fixed “mathematical estimator-safety benchmark,” without a named applied domain, external open problem, or comparator theorem whose use changes; this leaves the stated subfield kernel below the required field floor.

The text attributes a “positive endpoint tail-moment requirement” to Assumption 2, but Assumption 2 permits a limiting conditional law and requires bounded conditional moments; nondegeneracy is the separate α₊(0)+α₋(0)>0 condition used by Theorem 1.

The repeated field-novelty defect remained; the independent validity gate confirmed that the remaining broad exponent-class lever changes the claimed kernel. tldr: The fixed public quadratic propensity defines an exactly specified critical weak-overlap benchmark: treatment extremes have an exact Pareto design tail, while the linearly vanishing Bernoulli response has a critical-Gaussian inverse-weighted mean. On the full stipulated response class and identical original records, the target theorem couples the actual ET exponential dual and EL rational optimizer through a shared compensated Poisson source, transfers the genuine EL root on its moving pole domain, and proves a sharper actual EL-to-HT marked-mean expansion. ET has error scale \(n^{-1/3}\log n\); EL and clipped HT share the scale \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\). Total original-outcome intervals require uniform asymptotic coverage and sharp probability and expected lengths. This is a mathematical estimator-safety benchmark at subfield scope. Classical EL containment, scalar optimizer facts and generic heavy-tail and smooth-map ingredients are credited; empirical typicality and practical finite-sample coverage are not claimed.
gap: Pervin, Wang, and Kim, v1 Theorem 4.1/B.2, uses root-n dual localization; Kim (2009), Theorem 1, supplies regular calibration equivalence under a root-n ratio condition that the benchmark diagnostic checks fails. Neither supplies this infinite-score joint experiment. The exact ordinary mean EL reduction is already occupied. The residual theorem obligations are the localized moving-domain transfer with the shared empirical target, actual marked EL-to-HT remainder, and primitive same-record Poisson/Gaussian coupling. Final published misspecified-EL containment is partly externally unverifiable.
fill: Theorem 1 joins localized rational-root transfer, actual EL-to-HT rare-mark transfer and the primitive joint block with the credited ET smooth map. Theorems 2 and 3 deliver simultaneous same-class estimator orders and total data-only asymptotic inference with expected lengths. The scope is below field: no broader propensity class or empirical finite-sample reliability is established.
